items.title: Arturo O'Farrill interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2024
items.q: She wrote for Gary Valente, she wrote for me.

ctx.x: In your big band writing versus music for the dance, have you ever noticed that we depend sometimes on open solos, solo sections for individuals music-wise but also because they stretch out a composition. In the small instances where I’ve tried to write something — I’ll use the word “classical,” it’s alarming sometimes how much time you put into it and you play it and you’ve got 45 seconds so far, and you feel like okay give it to the soloists, stretch it out. Is that an issue for you?

No. It’s never been. As a matter of fact for me I like, without formerly knowing this I adopted the Ellingtonian model of understanding that the improvisation is an orchestrational compositional tool, not a chance to stretch a piece. In fact I’ve committed the cardinal sin of writing jazz pieces where there is no improvisation. So you know that doesn’t go so well with the DownBeat crowd but it works for me. I feel like I’ve written pieces where the improvisation must be utilitarian. It has to be. And I’m a lot…
